title: Procedural Marble Veining with Fracture Plane Reveal
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a procedural marble veining material system with an interactive fracture plane reveal, incorporating two loaded GLTF models.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 2, 5) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.3) and a directional light at (3, 5, 2) with intensity 1.0 and shadow mapping enabled.
- Set the renderer background to a dark grey (#1a1a2e). Enable tone mapping (ACESFilmic) and set outputColorSpace to SRGBColorSpace.
- Use OrbitControls for camera interaction.

ASSET LOADING:
- Load 'CesiumMan.glb' using GLTFLoader. Place it at position (-2, 0, 0). Scale it uniformly to 1.5. This model represents the 'intact specimen' that will receive the procedural marble material.
- Load 'DirectionalLight.glb' using GLTFLoader. Place it at position (2, 0, 0). Scale it uniformly to 1.0. This model represents the 'fractured specimen' that will show the fracture plane cross-section.
- After loading, traverse ALL meshes in both models and replace their materials with the custom procedural marble ShaderMaterial.

PROCEDURAL MARBLE SHADER:
- Create a custom ShaderMaterial with the following uniforms:
  - u_time (float, animated)
  - u_veinColor (vec3, default dark green: 0.05, 0.15, 0.05)
  - u_baseColor (vec3, default white: 0.95, 0.93, 0.88)
  - u_veinFrequency (float, default 3.0, range 1.0-10.0)
  - u_veinSharpness (float, default 5.0, range 1.0-20.0)
  - u_fractureProgress (float, default 0.0, range 0.0-1.0)
  - u_fracturePlaneY (float, default 0.5)
  - u_noiseOctaves (int, default 4)
- Vertex shader: pass world position, normal, and UV to fragment shader. Apply standard modelViewMatrix/projectionMatrix transforms.
- Fragment shader: Implement 3D Simplex or value noise (at least 4 octaves of fBm). Generate marble veining using sin(x * frequency + fbm(position) * amplitude) pattern. Mix baseColor and veinColor based on vein pattern. Add subtle subsurface scattering approximation using view-dependent fresnel term. When u_fractureProgress > 0, discard fragments above the fracture plane (worldPosition.y > u_fracturePlaneY * (1.0 - u_fractureProgress) + max_height * u_fractureProgress). On fragments near the fracture plane (within 0.05 units), render a cross-section color (slightly brighter, with denser vein pattern) to simulate the exposed interior.

FRACTURE PLANE REVEAL:
- The fracture plane is a horizontal clipping plane that progressively reveals the interior cross-section of the models.
- The fractured specimen (DirectionalLight.glb, right side) always shows the fracture at the current u_fractureProgress level.
- The intact specimen (CesiumMan.glb, left side) remains fully intact (fractureProgress=0) until the user explicitly applies fracture to it.

USER INTERACTIONS:
1. KEYBOARD 'V' key: Cycle vein color preset. Presets: dark green (0.05,0.15,0.05), dark red (0.3,0.02,0.02), dark blue (0.02,0.05,0.25), gold (0.4,0.3,0.05). Update u_veinColor on ALL marble materials. Track current preset index.
2. KEYBOARD 'F' key: Toggle fracture animation on the RIGHT model (DirectionalLight.glb). When toggled on, animate u_fractureProgress from 0 to 1 over 2 seconds. When toggled off, animate back from 1 to 0 over 2 seconds. Use smooth easing.
3. KEYBOARD 'G' key: Apply current fracture progress to the LEFT model (CesiumMan.glb) as well, syncing both models. Press again to reset left model fracture to 0.
4. SLIDER (DOM): A range input labeled 'Vein Frequency' controlling u_veinFrequency from 1.0 to 10.0 with step 0.1. Update in real-time on both models.
5. SLIDER (DOM): A range input labeled 'Vein Sharpness' controlling u_veinSharpness from 1.0 to 20.0 with step 0.5. Update in real-time.
6. BUTTON (DOM): 'Reset All' button that resets all uniforms to defaults, stops animations, and resets fracture progress to 0 on both models.
7. KEYBOARD ArrowUp/ArrowDown: Adjust u_fracturePlaneY by ±0.1 (clamped 0.0 to 2.0). This moves where the fracture cut happens.

HUD/UI:
- Position a semi-transparent panel (top-left, dark background, white text) showing:
  - Current vein color preset name
  - Current vein frequency value (1 decimal)
  - Current vein sharpness value (1 decimal)
  - Fracture progress percentage for each model (0-100%)
  - Fracture plane Y position
  - Models loaded status
- Place sliders and reset button below the info panel.

STATE MANAGEMENT (window.__3D_STATE__):
Expose and continuously update:
- modelsLoaded (boolean): true when BOTH glb models are loaded
- veinPresetIndex (int): current vein color preset index (0-3)
- veinPresetName (string): name of current preset ('green','red','blue','gold')
- veinFrequency (float): current vein frequency
- veinSharpness (float): current vein sharpness
- fractureProgressRight (float): fracture progress of right model (0.0-1.0)
- fractureProgressLeft (float): fracture progress of left model (0.0-1.0)
- fractureAnimating (boolean): whether fracture animation is currently running
- fractureDirection (string): 'opening' or 'closing' or 'idle'
- fracturePlaneY (float): current fracture plane Y position
- leftFractureSynced (boolean): whether left model fracture is synced to right
- meshCountLeft (int): number of meshes with marble material on left model
- meshCountRight (int): number of meshes with marble material on right model
- elapsedTime (float): total elapsed animation time
- cameraDistance (float): distance from camera to origin

ANIMATION:
- Animate u_time uniform each frame for subtle vein movement.
- Fracture animations should use smooth easing (ease-in-out).
- Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.

Ensure all models load with error handling. If a model fails to load, log the error and set a flag in __3D_STATE__.
physics_constraints: Fracture progress must be clamped [0,1]. Fracture plane Y must be clamped [0,2]. Vein frequency clamped [1,10]. Vein sharpness clamped [1,20]. All color components must remain in [0,1]. Fracture animation must complete in approximately 2 seconds. When synced, left fracture progress must equal right fracture progress within epsilon 0.01.
